name: BAGGS & MARSHALL RES - HOUSE

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, where a curved driveway branches off the road and winds through sparse desert scrub vegetation to reach the main residence and attached structures|The main residence is a multi-section single-story building with a dark hip roof, and a detached structure with a lighter roof is visible to the right|A small patch of green lawn is visible on the left side of the main structure|Scattered juniper trees surround the building cluster, with open desert terrain extending in all directions from the improved area.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from the east, with the road visible along the right edge of the frame and the residence positioned in the upper right of the property|A cleared, tan-colored graded area is visible to the left of the structures, consistent with a parking area or yard space|The surrounding terrain is flat to gently rolling desert with scattered low shrubs and juniper trees, providing no significant obstacles to cross-lot movement on the right side of the property.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where the back of the residence and a detached structure are visible with no fencing or walls enclosing the rear yard|The rear terrain transitions directly into open, undeveloped desert scrubland with widely spaced juniper trees, providing unobstructed access around the back of the structure|A cleared graded area is visible behind the main building cluster, and the road that serves as the property's front access is visible at the top of the frame.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property from the west, with the road running along the left edge of the frame and the main residence and detached structure clearly visible|The driveway approach from the road is visible, curving from the street toward the front of the building cluster|Open desert terrain with scattered juniper trees occupies the left side yard, and no fencing or walls restrict lateral movement along this side of the property.

considerations: The property is accessed via a single curved driveway that connects to the road at the front of the parcel, with a long approach through open desert terrain. The residence sits well back from the road, creating a long driveway approach for emergency vehicles. No fencing, gates, or perimeter walls are observed on any side, allowing unrestricted cross-lot movement around all sides of the structure. The surrounding terrain is open, flat to gently rolling desert scrub, and the open perimeter provides staging options on multiple sides of the building.
clarifications: Does the driveway surface support the weight of heavy emergency vehicles such as fire apparatus? Is there a secondary or alternate access route to the property beyond the single observed driveway connection to the road? Are there any gate or access controls at the driveway entrance that are not visible from the aerial imagery? Is the detached structure to the right of the main residence a garage, and if so, is it accessible from the driveway side?
